channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.content:encoded:

item.title: [6] An integrated theoretical and numerical approach to understand modern experiments on quantum magnetism
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Cristian D. Batista, Shiliang Li

Authors: Zi Yang Meng, Cristian D. Batista, Shiliang Li

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Perspective on bridging theory and experiment in quantum magnetism, which is a broader user interest.

Tags: #methodology #quantummagnetism

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03304-5 Models of quantum magnets have predicted many exciting phenomena that are yet to be observed. This Perspective argues that much tighter collaboration between analytical theory, numerics and experiments is needed to make progress.

item.title: [8] Surface d-orbital order in an intermetallic compound
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Zhijun Wang, Chaoyu Chen

Authors: Zhanyang Hao, Haohao Sheng, Wanru Ma, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Strongly relevant electronic structure study of orbital order in correlated intermetallic compounds.

Tags: #electronicstructure #intermetallic #orbitalorder

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03359-4 Whether orbital order can exist with a clear band-structure fingerprint in correlated materials has remained unresolved. Now an orbital order from rare earth 5d electrons without structural or magnetic order is seen in an intermetallic compound.
